items._modes: Whether a plan renews is the owner's choice in the console (plan_mode, schema §62). `a` is shown in the markup and says neither; marketing.js shows `aOnce` or `aRenew` when trial_offer() names the mode. `aRenew` must say "cancel anytime" (test:marketing).
items.a: Each plan card says what a plan costs, how long it lasts and what happens when it ends, before you pay, and checkout says it again. A plan is a year of the studio, from about {{fms:price.from.day}} a day, and your work stays in your browser either way.
items.aOnce: No. A plan is one payment for one year, from about {{fms:price.from.day}} a day. When the year ends nothing is charged: buy the next year when you want it, and your work stays in your browser either way, so there is nothing to cancel.
items.aRenew: Yes: a plan renews every year until you cancel, from about {{fms:price.from.day}} a day. Cancel anytime, in two taps, under Settings, Plan & purchases, Cancel auto-pay: nothing more is charged, and the plan runs to the end of the year you paid for. Your price is locked while you stay, and your bank or UPI app tells you before each charge.
items.aPay: Payment is through Razorpay, and checkout confirms the currency and the exact amount before you pay.
items.aPayUsd: Prices are in US dollars, paid through Razorpay, and the amount is confirmed at checkout before you pay.

items.a: Purchases are final, with three exceptions that are not discretionary: a duplicate or erroneous charge, a payment for a plan that was never activated on your account, and any refund the law of India requires. The Refund and Cancellation Policy has the detail.
items.aRenewNote: On auto-pay the same three cases apply to each charge, and cancelling stops the charges still to come without refunding the year already paid.

items.a: No. A plan is a year of the studio, and you pay the price of the day you buy it. The Dragon sample shows the studio filled in first.
items.aPass: No. While the launch offer lasts, {length} of the whole studio is {price}, once per account. {passTerms} After it, a plan costs what it costs on the day you buy it.

items.q: Which plan is right for me?
items.a: Basic is for writing: story, screenplay, drafts and import. Intermediate is for preparing the shoot: breakdown, storyboard, shot list, stripboard, budget, cast and crew, and sides. Pro adds call sheets, the AI tools and removal of branding. Each plan includes everything below it.

items.q: Can I move up a plan later?
items.a: Yes. Moving up mid-year credits the unused part of your current year against the new plan; moving down waits until your year ends. The work you have already done stays where it is either way.
No. There is no free plan. Whether purchases are required is a setting that can change, so the pricing page always shows what applies today.

items.q: Do I need a plan to try the sample films?
items.a: The Dragon sample project is there so you can see the studio filled in before you commit.

In your own browser, on your device, first. Once you are signed in, your films also sync to the studio's cloud so they reach your other devices, and row-level security limits each project to you and the people you share it with (a view link can read it, an edit link can change it). Anyone you share a project with can see its budget, unless you keep the budget private; then only you and people with an edit link can see the estimate, petty cash, crew payments and cost report. Figures typed into a blueprint's budget questions are not covered by that switch. You can switch sync off in Settings; the browser copy stays either way.

items.q: Does it work offline on a film set?
items.a: Yes. The studio installs like an app and caches itself, so you can keep writing, reordering the stripboard and printing call sheets when the signal drops, and what you changed is still there when you reconnect. It works on set without a signal for up to 14 days after you last signed in on that device, even opened from scratch. After that it needs a connection once, to check your sign-in and your plan again.

items.q: Can I get my work out?
items.a: Yes, in open formats. The screenplay exports as PDF, Word (.docx), Final Draft (.fdx) and Fountain from the Screenplay Writer's File menu. The breakdown's element index, the table read, script notes, the shot list, and the budget, actuals and expenses download as CSV, as do the edit log and the dialogue list on Pro, each on the plans that include that tool. A backup file holds every project and restores into any browser, and on Intermediate and Pro you can also back up to your own Google Drive.

items.q: Can I bring in a script from Final Draft or Fountain?
items.a: Yes. Import a Fountain, Final Draft, Word, text or PDF screenplay and the studio reads the scene headings, action, characters and dialogue into its own format. Scanned or encrypted PDFs are refused with a reason rather than guessed at.

items.q: Does the AI see my script?
items.a: Only if you choose to use the AI tools, which are optional and use your own key from a provider you pick. Nothing is sent to an AI provider unless you run one of those tools.
